model_reasoning: Macrostomia, or transverse facial cleft, results from the incomplete fusion of the maxillary and mandibular processes during embryonic development. These processes normally meet and fuse to form the corners of the mouth (oral commissures). If this fusion is incomplete, the mouth opening extends laterally beyond its normal boundaries, leading to an abnormally wide mouth.
